parsed.draft_response:
Hi there—thanks for the feature request. We understand you’d like to schedule weekly exports to be written directly to your S3 bucket, instead of downloading CSVs manually, and you estimate this would save your data team a couple of hours each week.

To confirm the exact setup you need, could you share a few details?
1) Which export(s) are you referring to (export type/source in our product)?
2) What schedule should we run (day/time) and which time zone?
3) How should the files land in S3 (folder/path convention and filename format)?
4) What should happen if an export runs again—overwrite the same file(s) or create new objects/versioned files?

Also, if you already have an S3 connection/credentials set up for exports, please let us know; if not, tell us what method you prefer (e.g., IAM role vs. access keys) so we can align on permissions.

Once we have the above, we can pass this to the appropriate team to evaluate feasibility and options for implementing scheduled S3 delivery. Since you mentioned this isn’t blocking, we’ll coordinate timeline and next steps based on your priorities.
promised_actions: Gather the requested details to clarify scope and implementation requirements
Escalate/escalate internally to the appropriate team for evaluation of scheduled exports to S3
Coordinate follow-up on options and timeline based on customer priorities
safety_notes: Avoid committing to feature availability or implementation timeline.
Avoid promising specific delivery semantics (overwrite/versioning, retries) without customer confirmation.
Request only minimum useful clarifications to define export type, schedule, S3 pathing, and delivery behavior.
